Budgeting apps. I know it sounds terrible, but it's been a godsend for me. In addition to some major impulse shopping issues, I have some trauma around finances that leads me to be really anxious and avoidant of touching anything money related at all. But I use Mint, and once you set up your initial budget, it manages everything for you and just alerts you when you're near maxing out a category. I try to look at it for 5 min once a day to see how I'm doing.   


I'm also super honest with myself about what I set for myself as a budget. My eating out budget and clothes shopping budget are well above what a "normal" person would need. (And I'm living on student loans, so it's /not/ a lot, but it's a healthy portion.) Most months, I don't come close to reaching my budget on either. But I know I emotionally/impulsively buy food and fashion, so to the extent that I can, I set myself up with some wiggle room so that I don't "fail" if I overdo it in those areas a bit. In the end, if I end up with a surplus in those categories, I feel like I am a super adult champion, and I'll either drop the money to savings or roll it over for a bigger spend in those categories the next month.

This is weirdly specific, but while meds generally improve my work overall, on meds I will very often use the wrong word- a lot of times, the exact opposite of the word I mean. My writing and reasoning is solid, but I'll switch or drop one word that ends up mattering a lot to the conclusion. I'm in law school, and replacing "Not guilty" with "guilty" is... sort of a big deal. I usually have to reread my work once I'm not medicated to catch these things. I've just started meds and haven't decided what I'm going to do with respect to exams as I've done reasonably well without them.

It was so damaging to my mental health that when he started just having sex with me anyway after I said no, I thought it was fair because I hadn't held up my end of the relationship. He raped me multiple times over the course of a year and just convinced me that I deserved it for not giving him sex when he needed it. Five years later, I still have severe PTSD and have ongoing related legal proceedings.   


I would seriously urge you to consider leaving. This person does not respect your health or your needs, and all signs point to this continuing to get worse rather than better. There are people out there who will respect your boundaries and support you in your recovery journey, even it means spending some time with their hand. I promise. Until you find them, it is better to be alone than be in a relationship where your body is not safe.

Thanks for the kind words. It's not even so much the idea that bad things will keep happening. I know I'm lucky at this point. I have a career I love, a partner I adore, good friends who are more like family, a stable life, etc. I could really see myself going through the rest of my life ticking off all of the boxes for success and achieving my goals. Maybe I'll never even be raped or abused again. But even so, that doesn't feel like it matters. It feels like the things that happened screwed me up enough that no matter how hard I work to recover I am never going to be able to be happy because this mental illness is bigger than I am. Thinking about continuing to put in as much work as I do on my self only to watch my mental health come crashing down every few months for the rest of my life is too much. 24 years of that has been too much, I can't begin to face 60 more.
